summary: Re-review after fixes. All 12 previously flagged issues were checked against the revised text; the major scapular-anastomosis error is corrected and the other 11 are resolved (compartment first-aid, ventrogluteal note, soleus wording, Trendelenburg vs waddling, posterior-dislocation radiography, triquetrum articulation, axillary nerve reasoning, rotator cuff worked example). The 10 changed units were re-read in full and every question was re-solved; all keys are correct, each MCQ has one defensible answer, and the new questions (PCL posterior drawer, humeral tubercle landmarks, knee spines, shoulder/acromion landmark, posterior dislocation view) are taught in their lessons. Only minor residual items remain, mainly cross-unit duplicates in units that were not changed. This is an AI review: the course still needs a subject-matter expert (anatomist/clinician) before clinical reliance.

issues.problem: Within-unit duplication was removed, but the unhappy-triad question still repeats across units (knee-leg-ankle-foot q005 asks the same thing), and the 82-year-old intracapsular femoral neck vignette is still near-identical in hip-thigh q008 and fracture-anatomy q004 (these units were not changed).
issues.suggestedFix: Keep one version of each and replace the other with a new item (for example femoral neck fracture types, subtrochanteric fracture, medial longitudinal arch collapse).

issues.problem: Objective 'Identify the normal bony landmarks on radiographs of the shoulder, wrist and knee' now has shoulder (q006) and knee (q004) landmark questions but none for the wrist.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one wrist landmark question (for example identifying the scaphoid, lunate or radial styloid on a PA view).

issues.problem: The pelvis/femur landmark objective is still covered by a single question (q001). This was flagged previously and the unit was not changed.
issues.suggestedFix: Add one or two landmark questions (for example greater and lesser trochanters, linea aspera, acetabular notch).
